Looking at the remaining hotspots: `EntityRendererMixin.onShouldRender` is consuming 0.11% with frustum culling checks, `DrawContext.onDrawString` at 0.08% is intercepting every string render call, and `BillboardParticle.onExtract` at 0.06% is doing frustum culling per particle. There's also `LocationMusicEngine.onEndTick()` at 0.06% running logic every tick, plus several smaller contributors like tooltip generation, text width calculations, and block entity rendering that are all adding up.

Now I'm seeing the rest of the performance profile — most of these are sub-0.02% hits from name tag modifications, entity glow effects, various tick handlers, and chat/network event listeners. The pattern is clear: lots of small overhead scattered across rendering, UI, and game logic systems.

Looking at the actual mixin implementations, I can spot several optimization opportunities. The `LevelRendererMixin` is creating new objects every frame when it should be reusing them, the `EntityRendererMixin` has redundant frustum culling that Minecraft already handles, and the `ParticleCullingMixin` is doing expensive lookups on every particle extraction. The `BlockEntityCullingMixin` is creating new AABB objects repeatedly, and the `LivingEntityRendererMixin` is using reflection every frame which is a major performance killer.

The real wins come from caching the `PoseStack` instead of recreating it, removing the duplicate frustum check since Minecraft already does this, storing the frustum reference directly instead of looking it up through the world renderer, reusing AABB objects with mutable updates, and caching reflection lookups statically so they only happen once.
